# Partial Pre-Rendering / Shell Analysis Report ## 1. Project structure overview Small **Next.js App Router** dashboard demo (no monorepo). | Item | Detail | |------|--------| | Framework | **Next.js `16.3.0-canary.80`** + **React 19.1.0** | | Router | App Router only (`/workspace/app`) | | Language | TypeScript | | Tests | Vitest present as dep; no app tests | **Key paths:** ``` /workspace/ ├── package.json ├── next.config.ts # cacheComponents (PPR successor) ├── tsconfig.json ├── opencode.json # agent eval config (not app code) ├── __agent_eval__/run.mjs # agent runner (not app code) └── app/ ├── layout.tsx # root HTML shell ├── page.tsx # dashboard (blocking fetch) ├── loading.tsx # route-level loading shell ├── CardStats.tsx # presentational ├── RevenueChart.tsx # presentational └── LatestInvoices.tsx # presentational ``` There is **no** `experimental.ppr` flag, no `Suspense` imports, and no files named “shell”. The PPR-related setup is **`cacheComponents: true`** plus a route-level **`loading.tsx`**. --- ## 2. Files related to PPR / shells / streaming ### Next.js config — Cache Components (PPR-era API) **`/workspace/next.config.ts`** ```1:7:/workspace/next.config.ts import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, } export default nextConfig ``` On Next.js 16 canaries, `cacheComponents` enables the Cache Components model (successor to experimental PPR): static parts can be prerendered; dynamic/async work is expected behind Suspense so a static shell can ship first. ### Route loading shell (implicit Suspense boundary) **`/workspace/app/loading.tsx`** ```1:8:/workspace/app/loading.tsx export default function Loading() { return (

Loading dashboard...

) } ``` This is the **only** loading/shell UI. Next treats `loading.tsx` as a Suspense fallback for the `page.tsx` segment. There are **no** nested `loading.tsx` files and **no** manual `` boundaries. ### Root layout (outer static chrome) **`/workspace/app/layout.tsx`** ```1:18:/workspace/app/layout.tsx import type { Metadata } from 'next' export const metadata: Metadata = { title: 'Create Next App', description: 'Generated by create next app', } export default function RootLayout({ children, }: Readonly<{ children: React.ReactNode }>) { return ( {children} ) } ``` Minimal root shell: `` / `` only. No nav, sidebar, or shared chrome that could form a richer prerendered shell. ### Page — single blocking data fetch (anti-pattern for shells) **`/workspace/app/page.tsx`** ```1:24:/workspace/app/page.tsx import { RevenueChart } from './RevenueChart' import { LatestInvoices } from './LatestInvoices' import { CardStats } from './CardStats' async function getDashboardData() { const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/dashboard') return res.json() } export default async function Page() { const data = await getDashboardData() return (

Dashboard

) } ``` ### Presentational children (no own fetch / no Suspense) **`/workspace/app/CardStats.tsx`** ```1:20:/workspace/app/CardStats.tsx export function CardStats({ totalRevenue, totalInvoices, }: { totalRevenue: number totalInvoices: number }) { return (

Total Revenue

${totalRevenue.toLocaleString()}

Total Invoices

{totalInvoices}

) } ``` **`/workspace/app/RevenueChart.tsx`** ```1:18:/workspace/app/RevenueChart.tsx export function RevenueChart({ revenue, }: { revenue: { month: string; amount: number }[] }) { return (

Revenue

    {revenue.map((item) => (
  • {item.month}: ${item.amount.toLocaleString()}
    • ))}
) } ``` **`/workspace/app/LatestInvoices.tsx`** ```1:18:/workspace/app/LatestInvoices.tsx export function LatestInvoices({ invoices, }: { invoices: { id: string; name: string; amount: number }[] }) { return (

Latest Invoices

    {invoices.map((invoice) => (
  • {invoice.name} - ${invoice.amount.toLocaleString()}
    • ))}
) } ``` ### Grep results (app source) | Pattern | Hits in app code | |---------|------------------| | `ppr` / `partialPreRendering` / `experimental.ppr` | **None** | | `Suspense` | **None** | | `use cache` / `"use cache"` | **None** | | `loading` shell | **`app/loading.tsx` only** | | `cacheComponents` | **`next.config.ts` only** | --- ## 3. How the current shell is structured (and what is unoptimized) ### Current rendering model ``` RootLayout (static: html/body) └── loading.tsx boundary (Suspense fallback for page) └── Page (async) ├── await getDashboardData() ← blocks entire page tree └── then render: h1 + CardStats + RevenueChart + LatestInvoices ``` **What acts as the “shell” today** 1. **Root layout** — empty chrome (`html`/`body`). 2. **`loading.tsx`** — full-page spinner: “Loading dashboard…”. 3. **No static page shell** — even `

Dashboard

` is behind the page-level await, so it is **not** part of an early static/prerendered shell. **What `cacheComponents: true` enables vs. what the app actually does** - Config is ready for Cache Components / static + dynamic holes. - The page still does **one top-level async fetch** and passes props into sync components. - That forces the segment to stay dynamic as a whole and only show the coarse `loading.tsx` fallback until **all** dashboard data is ready. - Child widgets cannot stream independently; there are no per-section fallbacks. ### Unoptimized aspects | Issue | Why it hurts shells / PPR | |-------|---------------------------| | **Blocking fetch at page root** | Nothing in `page.tsx` (including static title) can prerender or stream until the fetch finishes. | | **Single coarse `loading.tsx`** | One full-page spinner instead of layout-shaped skeletons for cards/chart/invoices. | | **No `` boundaries** | No granular “holes” for Cache Components / streaming. | | **Presentational-only children** | Data is not co-located; sections cannot suspend/stream on their own. | | **Monolithic API** | One `/dashboard` payload couples all sections to the slowest part of the response. | | **Minimal layout chrome** | No shared nav/sidebar that could always be in the static shell. | | **Spinner ≠ layout skeleton** | CLS and perceived performance worse than skeleton UI matching final structure. | | **No `"use cache"` / cache tags** | No explicit static caching of pure UI or cacheable data segments. | --- ## 4. `package.json` scripts and Next config **`/workspace/package.json`** ```1:23:/workspace/package.json { "private": true, "type": "module", "scripts": { "dev": "next dev", "build": "next build", "start": "next start" }, "dependencies": { "next": "^16.3.0-canary.80", "react": "19.1.0", "react-dom": "19.1.0" }, "devDependencies": { "@types/node": "^20", "@types/react": "^19", "@types/react-dom": "^19", "@vitejs/plugin-react": "^4.4.1", "typescript": "^5", "vite-tsconfig-paths": "^5.1.4", "vitest": "^3.1.3" } } ``` - Scripts: standard `dev` / `build` / `start` only (no analyze/export). - Next canary + React 19 aligns with Cache Components / modern streaming. - Config flag: **`cacheComponents: true`** (not legacy `experimental: { ppr: true }`). --- ## 5. Key layout / page / loading components that form the shell | Role | Path | Shell contribution | |------|------|--------------------| | Root layout | `/workspace/app/layout.tsx` | Static outer document only | | Loading shell | `/workspace/app/loading.tsx` | Full-route Suspense fallback (spinner) | | Page (dynamic hole) | `/workspace/app/page.tsx` | Entire dashboard content after one await | | Stats UI | `/workspace/app/CardStats.tsx` | No shell; data-bound presentational | | Chart UI | `/workspace/app/RevenueChart.tsx` | No shell; data-bound presentational | | Invoices UI | `/workspace/app/LatestInvoices.tsx` | No shell; data-bound presentational | --- ## Summary: current PPR shell implementation **Status:** PPR/Cache Components is **turned on in config**, but the app is **not structured to use a static shell effectively**. - **Enabled:** `cacheComponents: true` on Next 16.3 canary. - **Actual shell:** only root layout + a single route-level `loading.tsx` spinner. - **Main bottleneck:** `page.tsx` awaits one dashboard fetch before rendering anything, including static UI. - **No** manual Suspense, nested loading UI, `"use cache"`, or independent async server components per widget. ### Optimization opportunities (conceptual) 1. **Static shell first** — Keep `

Dashboard

…structure…
` (and richer layout chrome) outside any await so it can prerender as the static shell. 2. **Granular Suspense** — Wrap each section (`CardStats`, `RevenueChart`, `LatestInvoices`) in `` with async server children that fetch their own data. 3. **Replace or refine `loading.tsx`** — Prefer layout-matching skeletons per section; keep route `loading.tsx` only as a coarse fallback if needed. 4. **Split fetches** — Per-widget endpoints or parallel fetches inside each suspended component so sections stream independently. 5. **Optional `"use cache"`** — Cache pure static UI / stable data under Cache Components rules. 6. **Richer root/layout chrome** — Nav/sidebar in layout so the prerendered shell is useful before dynamic holes fill in. **Bottom line:** This repo is a minimal dashboard fixture that **advertises** Cache Components via config but still uses a **monolithic page fetch + single loading spinner**, so almost none of the static-shell / streaming benefits of PPR-style rendering are realized yet. session_id: ses_0bcd97194ffetLshL8MmK3619B

sections cannot suspend/stream on their own. | | **Monolithic API** | One `/dashboard` payload couples all sections to the slowest part of the response. | | **Minimal layout chrome** | No shared nav/sidebar that could always be in the static shell. | | **Spinner ≠ layout skeleton** | CLS and perceived performance worse than skeleton UI matching final structure. | | **No `"use cache"` / cache tags** | No explicit static caching of pure UI or cacheable data segments. | --- ## 4. `package.json` scripts and Next config **`/workspace/package.json`** ```1:23:/workspace/package.json { "private": true, "type": "module", "scripts": { "dev": "next dev", "build": "next build", "start": "next start" }, "dependencies": { "next": "^16.3.0-canary.80", "react": "19.1.0", "react-dom": "19.1.0" }, "devDependencies": { "@types/node": "^20", "@types/react": "^19", "@types/react-dom": "^19", "@vitejs/plugin-react": "^4.4.1", "typescript": "^5", "vite-tsconfig-paths": "^5.1.4", "vitest": "^3.1.3" } } ``` - Scripts: standard `dev` / `build` / `start` only (no analyze/export). - Next canary + React 19 aligns with Cache Components / modern streaming. - Config flag: **`cacheComponents: true`** (not legacy `experimental: { ppr: true }`). --- ## 5. Key layout / page / loading components that form the shell | Role | Path | Shell contribution | |------|------|--------------------| | Root layout | `/workspace/app/layout.tsx` | Static outer document only | | Loading shell | `/workspace/app/loading.tsx` | Full-route Suspense fallback (spinner) | | Page (dynamic hole) | `/workspace/app/page.tsx` | Entire dashboard content after one await | | Stats UI | `/workspace/app/CardStats.tsx` | No shell; data-bound presentational | | Chart UI | `/workspace/app/RevenueChart.tsx` | No shell; data-bound presentational | | Invoices UI | `/workspace/app/LatestInvoices.tsx` | No shell; data-bound presentational | --- ## Summary: current PPR shell implementation **Status:** PPR/Cache Components is **turned on in config**, but the app is **not structured to use a static shell effectively**. - **Enabled:** `cacheComponents: true` on Next 16.3 canary. - **Actual shell:** only root layout + a single route-level `loading.tsx` spinner. - **Main bottleneck:** `page.tsx` awaits one dashboard fetch before rendering anything, including static UI. - **No** manual Suspense, nested loading UI, `"use cache"`, or independent async server components per widget. ### Optimization opportunities (conceptual) 1. **Static shell first** — Keep `

Dashboard

…structure…
` (and richer layout chrome) outside any await so it can prerender as the static shell. 2. **Granular Suspense** — Wrap each section (`CardStats`, `RevenueChart`, `LatestInvoices`) in `` with async server children that fetch their own data. 3. **Replace or refine `loading.tsx`** — Prefer layout-matching skeletons per section; keep route `loading.tsx` only as a coarse fallback if needed. 4. **Split fetches** — Per-widget endpoints or parallel fetches inside each suspended component so sections stream independently. 5. **Optional `"use cache"`** — Cache pure static UI / stable data under Cache Components rules. 6. **Richer root/layout chrome** — Nav/sidebar in layout so the prerendered shell is useful before dynamic holes fill in. **Bottom line:** This repo is a minimal dashboard fixture that **advertises** Cache Components via config but still uses a **monolithic page fetch + single loading spinner**, so almost none of the static-shell / streaming benefits of PPR-style rendering are realized yet. session_id: ses_0bcd97194ffetLshL8MmK3619B
